The talks follow an essay Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published Saturday, calling on the industry to work together to pace frontier development and avoid catastrophic risks. Sam Altman, Google’s Demis Hassabis, and Elon Musk each publicly backed elements of that call.
This comes as Altman says OpenAI would join Anthropic in embedding third-party evaluators to monitor model safety. Readers curious about the executive driving this push can find more on
in prior coverage.

Some participants, including Altman, have flagged that coordination among direct competitors could raise antitrust concerns. Lehane pushed back on that framing directly, saying OpenAI does not believe the three companies need a government antitrust waiver to coordinate on safety matters.

Independent Checks and the FRONTIER Act

OpenAI is backing a key provision of the bipartisan FRONTIER Act that would require leading AI developers to allow independent third-party organizations to assess their models and safety practices, according to POLITICO.

Lehane also said OpenAI supports a provision in the proposed FRONTIER Act that would require top frontier labs to admit independent verification organizations, external groups tasked with assessing whether advanced models are being developed safely. That positions the current talks alongside a live legislative debate over third-party audits versus industry self-policing.

The primary evidence doesn’t establish a binding agreement, formal charter, or detailed operating terms between the three labs. What’s confirmed is narrower: ongoing conversations, public statements of support, and one specific legislative endorsement from OpenAI’s policy chief.
